description: A benefit plan deduction and an earned wage advance recovery are deductions from net pay, not statutory contributions. Year-end annualization reads contributions from payslip lines; Phase 24 excluded the LOAN-, EWA- and BEN- code families before the label is read but proved only loans end to end. A voluntary savings plan is labelled 'Benefit, <plan name>' (code BEN-<plan id>), and a plan named after an agency ('Pag-IBIG MP2 Savings', 'SSS WISP Flexi-Fund') matched the contribution label test, so before the Phase 24 exclusion its deductions were summed as contributions, a non-taxable bucket, and inflated the refund. Phase 26 certifies the behaviour through the real engine with three workers hired at the switch on the same salary: a control, a worker on two agency-named voluntary savings plans, and a worker whose earned wage advance is recovered every cutoff. Every worker's year-end settlement must equal the control's.

sources.bir: BIR RR 11-2018 as amended by TRAIN: semi-monthly withholding table effective 2023 onward (up to 10,417 exempt; 10,417 to 16,667: 15%; 16,667 to 33,333: 937.50 + 20%; over 33,333: 4,270.70 + 25% of the excess); annual table (up to 250,000 exempt; 250,000 to 400,000: 15% of the excess over 250,000). Only the employee's mandatory SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG contributions are excluded from taxable compensation (NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(f)). A voluntary savings plan contribution and the recovery of an advance already paid are the employee's own money and are not such contributions.
sources.thirteenthMonth: Presidential Decree 851: 13th month pay = one twelfth of basic salary earned in the year; exempt up to 90,000 together with other benefits (NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(e)).

assumptions: Tax year 2026, 24 semi-monthly cutoffs, 'split' timing, monthly salary 60,000 (30,000 a cutoff), every worker hired 2026-07-01 so only the 12 engine cutoffs 13-24 exist and there are no imported rows. An ordinary cutoff: gross 30,000; SSS 875, PhilHealth 750, Pag-IBIG 100 (1,725); taxable 30,000 - 1,725 = 28,275; withholding 937.50 + 0.20 x (28,275 - 16,667) = 3,259.10. Benefit shares and advance recoveries are taken from net pay after tax, so they change net pay and nothing else in the cutoff.

A benefit employee share is the enrolment's monthly contribution divided by two per cutoff (capped by the plan cap, which is above the contribution here). An advance is recovered all-or-nothing as requested amount plus fee; disposable pay never limits either deduction.
A fresh advance is approved before every cutoff and marked repaid after it, which is what release settlement does; the release approval workflow itself is not part of this certification.

Year end for a worker with no 13th month paid: entries 12 x 30,000; entitlement = basic earned 360,000 / 12 = 30,000 is accrued unpaid and added to gross compensation; contributions 12 x 1,725 = 20,700 and ONLY those; the 30,000 sits inside the 90,000 pool; non-taxable = exempt pool + contributions; taxable = gross - non-taxable; tax = 15% x (taxable - 250,000); withheld = the sum of the WHT lines only; a refund is a negative adjustment.

noDeductionControl.description: No benefit plan and no advance. Net pay 25,015.90 in every cutoff. Year end: gross 360,000 + 30,000 accrued = 390,000; non-taxable 30,000 + 20,700 = 50,700; taxable 339,300; tax 15% x 89,300 = 13,395.00; withheld 12 x 3,259.10 = 39,109.20; refund 25,714.20.

agencyNamedSavingsPlans.description: Two voluntary savings plans named after an agency: 'Pag-IBIG MP2 Savings' at 1,000.00 a month (500.00 a cutoff) and 'SSS WISP Flexi-Fund' at 600.00 a month (300.00 a cutoff), 800.00 a cutoff and 9,600.00 over the 12 cutoffs. Cutoff net pay 25,015.90 - 800.00 = 24,215.90; gross, SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG and withholding are the control's. Year end must equal the control: statutory contributions 20,700 (NOT 30,300), non-taxable 50,700, taxable 339,300, tax 13,395.00, refund 25,714.20. If the savings deductions were counted as contributions: non-taxable 60,300, taxable 329,700, tax 15% x 79,700 = 11,955.00 and a refund 1,440.00 too large (27,154.20).

wageAdvanceEveryCutoff.description: An approved earned wage advance of 2,000.00 plus a 50.00 fee is recovered in every cutoff 13-24 (2,050.00 a cutoff, 24,600.00 in all). Cutoff net pay 25,015.90 - 2,050.00 = 22,965.90. The recovery line is labelled 'Earned wage advance recovery' under the code EWA-<id>; year end must equal the control: contributions 20,700, taxable 339,300, tax 13,395.00, refund 25,714.20. The recovered amount is never a contribution and never reduces taxable income.

limitations: Benefit plans are exercised only as voluntary employee-share deductions with no dependants and no employer share; an HMO, an insurance plan or a benefit that credits the 90,000 pool is not exercised.
An earned wage advance is exercised only as a full recovery in every cutoff; a deferred recovery (disposable pay too low) and the settlement transaction itself are not exercised.
One salary, 'split' timing, a worker hired at the switch (no imported history), deductions that are never limited by disposable pay.
Final pay (separation) reads contributions by exact code and is not affected by the label defect; it is not exercised here.
Year-end rows already computed under an older rule are replaced only when year end is recomputed.
